title: Actuator
description: What drives a joint. The one field that matters most is the one datasheets rarely publish: continuous_torque_nm. A hobby servo's headline number is stall torque - what it produces at the instant it stops moving, drawing a current it cannot sustain - and a model that reads it as capacity will confidently specify a mechanism that overheats. Only the continuous figure feeds a capacity derivation (ADR-0004).

part_id.description: The OpenPartsCore entry for this actuator, if it has one. Stored, not resolved (ADR-0006).

type.description: hobby-servo takes a PWM pulse and reports nothing. smart-servo has a bus and position feedback. The distinction matters for what a controller can know, not only for what the motor can do.

stall_torque_nm.description: The datasheet headline, as a CURVE SAMPLED AT VOLTAGES rather than one figure (ADR-0014). Recorded because datasheets publish it and omitting the field invites someone to write it into continuous_torque_nm, NOT because it is usable. A validator must refuse to let these values reach a capacity derivation (ADR-0004).

continuous_torque_nm.description: The only torque that may feed a capacity derivation, and an array for the reason ADR-0014 gives: torque against voltage is a curve, and this actuator's own rated range can span 26%. Null means capacity cannot be derived and the answer is 'incomplete', naming this actuator - the same shape as OpenBuildCore answering 'requires slicing' for a machine with no measured throughput (its ADR-0005). Most hobby datasheets do not publish this, so null will be the common case; that is a true statement about the available evidence, not a gap to be filled with a fraction of stall torque.

how_determined.description: Datasheet continuous rating, or a measurement and its method. A rule of thumb applied to stall torque is not a determination and must be rejected here - it is a guess wearing a citation.

thermal_basis.description: Duty cycle, ambient, and whether steady state was reached. A torque held for ten seconds is not a continuous torque.

holding_torque_nm.description: The stepper/BLDC datasheet headline, indexed by current (ADR-0023). The enum accepted 'stepper' and 'bldc' long before any field could express one: every torque row required at_volts, so recording a stepper honestly was impossible and inventing a voltage was the only way through - which is the failure this repo exists to refuse. STILL FEEDS NO DERIVATION. Whether a holding torque may size a mechanism is NOT decided here: the datasheet read for ADR-0023 does not say whether it is sustainable, and continuous_torque_nm remains the only torque that may (ADR-0004).

stall_force_n.description: The linear-actuator datasheet headline, in NEWTONS (ADR-0025). Actuonix calls it 'Max Force (lifted)'. Recorded because datasheets publish it and omitting the field invites someone to write a force into a torque field, NOT because it is usable: like stall torque it may never reach a capacity derivation (ADR-0004).

continuous_force_n.description: Force a linear actuator can sustain. The ONLY force that may size a mechanism, exactly as continuous_torque_nm is for rotary ones (ADR-0004, ADR-0025). Expect null: the Actuonix L12 publishes a 20% max duty cycle, which is a vendor saying in as many words that its published forces are not continuous.

how_determined.description: A fraction of the stall force is not a determination, for the same reason it is not one for torque.

no_load_speed_rad_s.description: Also voltage-indexed (ADR-0014): the same datasheet that publishes three torque rows publishes three speed rows, from the same table.

travel.description: The actuator's own travel, before any gearing. Distinct from the joint limits in the robot record: those are what the mechanism permits, this is what the motor can do. A capacity or reachability derivation takes the tighter of the two.

backlash_rad.description: Absent means UNKNOWN, never zero. Backlash is why a commanded pose and an achieved pose differ, and recording it as zero because nobody measured it is the invented-data failure in miniature. NOTE: two vendors' figures are not comparable without their methods, and this is now PRIMARY-SOURCED ON BOTH SIDES. Nabtesco writes that 'many gearbox manufacturers choose to use the standard definition of backlash, which is just the amount of free travel between parts', contrasting its own, which 'includes not only the mechanical gap between parts, but also ... the amount of angular displacement that occurs due to loading the gearbox'. Harmonic Drive is one of the manufacturers so described: 'the backlash in an assembled component set is defined as pure play existing between the input and output', 'measured at output with input locked'. The two do not differ by a percentage - they publish NON-CORRESPONDING QUANTITIES. Nabtesco reads lost motion at 3% of rated torque; Harmonic Drive names no applied torque and handles the low-torque region separately as a three-region spring rate. Neither converts into the other. The related specifics - four-point averaging, and which percentage each vendor applies - remain unsourced. ANSI/AGMA 2002 covers tooth thickness and backlash in a gear MESH, which is a different quantity from an assembled reducer's output-shaft figure; its scope text is paywalled and was not read. Still licenses no value: absent means UNKNOWN (ADR-0018, ADR-0021).

measured_efficiency.description: Replaces a scalar efficiency field, which was the third instance of this repo's recurring defect: a quantity varying over an operating envelope, stored as one number (ADR-0018). Harmonic Drive's own engineering data states efficiency 'varies depending on input speed, ratio, load level, temperature, and type of lubrication' and publishes eight curves and no scalar - and its worked example lands at 58% at rated load and 50% at 60% of rated, against the 80-90% the trade literature quotes. STILL FEEDS NO DERIVATION, and now for a sourced reason rather than an unmodelled one: efficiency curves describe a gearbox that is TURNING, indexed by input speed, while a static hold has an input speed of zero. Applying a running efficiency to a held pose is wrong in kind, not in value. A vendor curve may be sampled into this array; a single catalogue number may not, because there is no such thing.

input_speed_rad_s.description: The operating point this figure was read at. Required, because it is the primary index of every published efficiency curve.

output_torque_nm.description: Efficiency falls with load below rated; a figure without its load is not a figure.

lubricant.description: Named grease or oil, and quantity where the vendor conditions the curve on it. Harmonic Drive's curves are valid only for their own grease at standard quantity.

how_determined.description: Read from which chart of which document, or measured how. Reading a value off a chart image is not a citation and should say so.

starting_torque_nm.description: Input torque required to begin motion. A RANGE, never a value (ADR-0021) - Harmonic Drive publishes 3-50 N.cm for one size, spanning better than an order of magnitude, and the variation is unit-to-unit rather than over an operating envelope. FEEDS NO DERIVATION.

backdriving_torque_nm.description: Output torque required to turn the input - what a stationary geartrain resists. A RANGE, never a value (ADR-0021), and THE TWO ENDS ANSWER OPPOSITE QUESTIONS. 'Can this hold a load unpowered' is answered by the MINIMUM, because your unit might be the loose one. 'Will this back-drive when I need it to, for hand-guiding or a fault that must not lock the joint' is answered by the MAXIMUM, because your unit might be the stiff one. A single figure cannot serve both and picking an end silently is wrong in one direction depending on a question this record does not know the caller is asking. FEEDS NO DERIVATION: the tempting inference - that a load below the backdriving minimum is held with no actuator torque - is a physical claim this repo has no source for, and its failure mode is a joint that lets go.

torque_limit.description:
A CEILING on what may be applied to the output, never a torque the actuator can deliver (ADR-0027). Pololu publishes, for the whole 25D family and identically at every ratio, 'the recommended upper limit for continuously applied loads is 4 kg-cm' and an intermittent limit of 8 kg-cm. That it does not change with ratio or power tier is what proves it describes the GEARTRAIN rather than the motor's heating.

It may never become continuous_torque_nm. 'Do not exceed X' and 'can sustain X' are different claims, and at low ratios the ceiling sits ABOVE the motor's stall torque - 4 kg-cm against 3.9 at 9.7:1 - where treating it as a capacity would promise a torque the motor cannot produce at all.

What it CAN do is refuse. A required torque above this ceiling is a sound no, the same asymmetry ADR-0015 rests on: static capacity is sound negative and no combination of it yields a provable yes.

continuous_nm.description: The vendor's recommended upper limit for a continuously applied load. An upper bound, not an achievable value.

intermittent_nm.description: Where the vendor publishes a separate, higher limit for intermittent loads. Must not be below continuous_nm.

how_determined.description: The vendor's own words where they have them, and a how_determined that states nothing is refused (ADR-0026).

feedback.description: 'none' is a real answer and a consequential one: an open-loop actuator cannot confirm it reached a commanded pose, so anything derived about where the mechanism actually is becomes an assumption.

stall_current_a.description: Sizing a supply from no-load current is how a mechanism browns out the moment it takes a load.

mass_g.description: An actuator mounted partway along a chain is itself a load on every joint below it.

duty_cycle_pct.description: The vendor's stated maximum duty cycle, as a percentage (ADR-0025). Distinct from thermal_basis, which is prose about how ONE continuous figure was determined and therefore has nowhere to live when there is no continuous row. This is a statement about the actuator itself: the L12's 'Max Duty Cycle 20%' is the vendor explaining why its published forces are not continuous ratings. ABSENT MEANS UNKNOWN, never 100.

basis.description: Whether this value describes the PRODUCT LINE or the object on your bench (ADR-0018). The distinction is not pedantry: Harmonic Drive states in a datasheet that its published torsional stiffness is 'the average of many tests of actual units' and that 'the spring rate of an individual unit may vary within approximately +/-30% of the average'. A cited value has meant 'somebody published it' everywhere in this platform so far; this is a vendor saying their number describes a population. ABSENT MEANS UNKNOWN, never 'assumed exact' - and a derivation must report the weakest basis it consumed, because a verdict built from population averages is a different claim from one built from measurements of the specific hardware.

torqueRange.description: A quantity that varies UNIT TO UNIT rather than over an operating envelope, so it is stored as a range and never collapsed to a value (ADR-0021). There is deliberately no 'typical' field: it would be read as the answer, the range would become decoration, and a vendor-published midpoint does not exist - inventing one would be a number with no source sitting between two that have one.

how_determined.description: The vendor's method where they state one - Harmonic Drive's reads 'based on actual tests with the component sets assembled in their housings, and inclusive of friction resistance of oil seals, and churning of oil', which is the reference example of the standard this repo asks for. ALSO RECORD THE ORIGINAL UNITS if a conversion happened: a figure published in N.cm converts to _nm on the way in, and a reader checking against the datasheet will be looking for N.cm.

spreadPct.description: Unit-to-unit variation the vendor states for a model-typical figure, as a percentage of the value. Only ever a figure somebody published; absent means the spread is UNKNOWN, not zero.

torqueAtVolts.description: One row of a published table. Voltage is not an annotation on the value - it is the index the value is looked up by, and a derivation that picks the wrong row is wrong by the width of the curve (ADR-0014).

at_volts.description: Required. A torque or speed figure without its supply voltage is not a figure - the same servo quoted at 6.0 V and 7.4 V differs substantially, and the XM430 spans 26% across its own rated range.

at_amps.description: Current drawn at this row, where the datasheet states it. Sizing a supply from no-load current is how a mechanism browns out the moment it takes a load.

torqueAtAmps.description: A torque figure indexed by CURRENT, for an actuator whose torque is set by current rather than supply voltage (ADR-0023). Deliberately has no at_volts: a stepper datasheet's 'rated voltage' is rated current times phase resistance and carries no information the other two rows do not. A real supply voltage belongs in electrical.

at_amps.description: Required, per phase. This is the index a row is looked up by, the way at_volts is for a servo. A holding torque without the current it was measured at is not a figure.

forceAtVolts.description: A force figure indexed by voltage, for an actuator whose output is LINEAR (ADR-0025). Force is not torque and newtons are not newton-metres; the two families of field are kept apart so a unit error cannot be written down as an ordinary value.

at_volts.description: Required, and the index. The L12 is sold in 6 V and 12 V variants whose force figures differ, so a force without its voltage is not a figure - the same rule ADR-0014 established for torque.
